Pranav, come here. You have the same face your Kiran Chacha had after Class 10 results. Let me tell you what I did.
Everyone said, take science, you got good marks. My friends were taking commerce. I didn't know what I wanted.
So I made a table in my rough notebook. Four columns: how much I like it, jobs later, how hard it is for me, how far the college is. I thought, liking matters most, so I gave it three points of weight. Jobs two, effort two, distance one.
Then I scored science, commerce and arts from one to five on each. Multiplied, added. Arts came out on top, because history made my heart race and the college was close. My father was shocked. But when he saw the table, he said, "At least you thought about it."
Look at me now, beta. History teacher, thirty years, never bored a single day.

qa.q: How many points of weight did Kiran give to liking the subject?
qa.a: Kiran gave it three points of weight.

qa.q: How might Kiran have felt when arts came out on top?
qa.a: He probably felt relieved and excited, since history made his heart race, though a little nervous about his father's reaction.

qa.q: At the point his father was shocked, what else could Kiran have done, and how might it have gone?
qa.a: He could have dropped the table and taken science to please everyone, but he would likely have ended up in work that bored him.

qa.q: How did Kiran's father see the table?
qa.a: His father was shocked at first, but seeing the table made him accept that Kiran had thought about it carefully.

The stream form had to reach the school office by ten the next morning, and the power in Baljeet's lane had gone at seven. By the light of a phone torch, he ruled a table in the back of his chemistry notebook.
Down the side: science, commerce, arts. Across the top: interest, job outlook, effort for me, college distance. He thought hard. Interest mattered most to him, so that got weight three. Jobs, two. Effort and distance, one each.
He scored each from one to five, multiplied, added. Science 38, commerce 33, arts 29.
His older brother Shankar leaned over. "Science? You were saying commerce all week."
"I thought so too. But I gave commerce a two for interest. I don't actually enjoy accounts."
Shankar nodded slowly. "Then tick science."

qa.q: How might Baljeet have felt when the totals showed science ahead?
qa.a: He was probably surprised but settled, since the table showed he didn't actually enjoy accounts.

qa.q: What else could Baljeet do before handing in the form, and why?
qa.a: He could talk to a science teacher or senior about the workload, to check that his effort score was realistic.

qa.q: How does Shankar see his brother's table?
qa.a: Shankar is surprised at first, since Baljeet talked about commerce all week, but accepts the reasoning and tells him to tick science.
